topics.title: Properties of Rational Numbers
objectives: Student can identify if rational numbers are closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division
Student can apply commutative and associative properties to simplify calculations involving rational numbers
Student can state the roles of zero and one as additive and multiplicative identities respectively
visualIdeas: a grid table with operations as columns and number systems as rows, populated with green checkmarks and red crosses for closure
an animation of terms swapping places with a curved arrow to illustrate commutativity

topics.title: Distributivity and Inverse
objectives: Student can find the additive inverse and multiplicative inverse of a given rational number
Student can calculate products of rational numbers using the distributive property of multiplication over addition
visualIdeas: a number line highlighting a number and its negative at equal distances from zero
the distributive formula with colored arrows distributing a factor to two terms inside parentheses

topics.title: Solving Equations having the Variable on both Sides
objectives: Student can solve linear equations in one variable where the variable terms appear on both sides
Student can construct and solve linear equations representing word problems about numbers, ages, or currencies
visualIdeas: a balance scale with variable boxes and unit weights on both sides, showing the step-by-step subtraction of boxes from one side
a two-column table comparing the verbal phrases of a word problem with their corresponding algebraic expressions

topics.title: Reducing Equations to Simpler Form
objectives: Student can solve complex linear equations by clearing fractions and parentheses
Student can apply cross-multiplication to reduce equations of the form (ax + b)/(cx + d) = k to a linear form
visualIdeas: a step-by-step algebraic simplification where the least common multiple is multiplied with every term, highlighted in red
a diagonal arrows overlay showing the cross-multiplication of numerator and denominator

topics.title: Polygons and Classification
objectives: Student can classify curves as open, closed, simple, or non-simple
Student can categorize polygons based on the number of vertices or sides
Student can differentiate between convex and concave polygons as well as regular and irregular polygons
visualIdeas: a classification chart showing shapes grouped under convex and concave with diagonals drawn to show if they lie outside the shape
a comparison side-by-side of a regular hexagon with equal sides/angles and an irregular hexagon

topics.title: Angle Sum Properties
objectives: Student can calculate the sum of interior angles of any polygon with n sides using the formula (n-2) x 180 degrees
Student can solve for unknown interior angles in given polygons
visualIdeas: a pentagon divided into three triangles by drawing diagonals from a single vertex, showing how the sum is 3 x 180 degrees
a worked geometric problem where an unknown angle x in a pentagon is solved step-by-step

topics.title: Sum of the Measures of the Exterior Angles
objectives: Student can state that the sum of the exterior angles of any polygon is 360 degrees
Student can calculate the measure of each exterior angle of a regular polygon with n sides
visualIdeas: a polygon with its sides extended in a clockwise direction, showing the exterior angles colored to form a complete circle of 360 degrees
a step-by-step formula derivation for the exterior angle of a regular octagon

topics.title: Kinds of Quadrilaterals
objectives: Student can identify the defining properties of a trapezium, a kite, and a parallelogram
Student can apply properties of sides, angles, and diagonals of a parallelogram to find unknown lengths and angles
visualIdeas: a family tree diagram of quadrilaterals branching into trapezium, kite, and parallelogram
a parallelogram with opposite sides marked equal, opposite angles marked equal, and consecutive angles shown as supplementary

topics.title: Special Parallelograms
objectives: Student can list the special properties of a rhombus, a rectangle, and a square
Student can apply the diagonal properties of special parallelograms to calculate missing lengths and perpendicularity
visualIdeas: a Venn diagram showing the nested relationship between parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, and squares
a diagram of a rhombus showing its diagonals bisecting each other at a right angle symbol

topics.title: Organising and Grouping Data
objectives: Student can construct a frequency distribution table with tally marks for a given raw data set
Student can group raw data into class intervals and identify lower limits, upper limits, and class width
visualIdeas: a split screen showing a list of numbers on the left and a tally table filling up on the right
a diagram highlighting the upper limit, lower limit, and size of a class interval like 20-30

topics.title: Bars with a Difference (Histograms)
objectives: Student can construct a histogram for a grouped frequency distribution
Student can interpret data presented in a histogram, including identifying intervals with peak frequencies
visualIdeas: a histogram showing adjacent bars with no spaces between them, highlighting the continuous nature of the x-axis
a histogram with a jagged line (broken line) near the origin to show a jump in scale

topics.title: Circle Graph or Pie Chart
objectives: Student can calculate the central angle of sectors in a pie chart given categorical data percentages or fractions
Student can construct a pie chart using a protractor and compass to represent a given dataset
Student can interpret information from a given pie chart to answer comparative questions
visualIdeas: a circular pizza with slices representing different data proportions alongside a table calculating central angles
a protractor aligned to a circle's radius showing how to draw a sector of exactly 120 degrees

topics.title: Chance and Probability
objectives: Student can list all possible outcomes of a simple random experiment like flipping a coin or rolling a die
Student can calculate the probability of a specific event using the formula: Number of favorable outcomes divided by the Total number of outcomes
visualIdeas: a spinning wheel with colored sectors, showing the outcomes as a fraction
a tree diagram showing the two branches of a coin flip (Heads and Tails) with 1/2 probability annotated on each

topics.title: Properties of Square Numbers
objectives: Student can determine if a number is a perfect square by analyzing its unit digit
Student can state the pattern relating the number of zeros at the end of a square number to its square root
visualIdeas: a table of numbers 1 to 20 with their squares, highlighting unit digits in yellow
a visual grid of square arrays showing the sum of consecutive odd numbers forming perfect squares

topics.title: Finding Squares and Pythagorean Triplets
objectives: Student can calculate the square of a large number without actual multiplication using algebraic expansion
Student can generate a Pythagorean triplet when given one of its members using the general form (2m, m^2 - 1, m^2 + 1)
visualIdeas: an algebraic splitting of 42 squared into (40+2) squared, solved step-by-step using binomial expansion
a right-angled triangle with side lengths corresponding to a generated Pythagorean triplet

topics.title: Square Roots by Prime Factorisation
objectives: Student can define the square root as the inverse operation of squaring
Student can calculate the square root of a perfect square using the prime factorisation method
Student can determine the smallest number by which a given non-perfect square must be multiplied or divided to make it a perfect square
visualIdeas: a factor tree showing prime factors grouped in pairs of two
a mathematical division stack showing prime factorisation with paired primes circled

topics.title: Square Roots by Division Method
objectives: Student can calculate the square root of large numbers using the long division method
Student can estimate the square root of a non-perfect square to the nearest whole number
visualIdeas: a step-by-step animated layout of the square root long division showing how digits are paired under bars
a comparison scale placing a non-perfect square between its two closest perfect square neighbors

topics.title: Square Roots of Decimals
objectives: Student can calculate the square root of a decimal number using the long division method with correct placement of decimal points
Student can apply square roots to solve real-life geometry problems involving areas of squares
visualIdeas: a decimal square root long division showing the placement of bars on integral parts and decimal parts
a square field diagram labeled with its area, showing the arrow transition to its side length via square root

topics.title: Cubes and Perfect Cubes
objectives: Student can identify perfect cubes by checking if prime factors can be grouped in triplets
Student can calculate the smallest number that must be multiplied or divided by a number to make it a perfect cube
visualIdeas: a comparison diagram showing a 1x1x1 cube, 2x2x2 cube, and 3x3x3 cube built of unit blocks
prime factor grouping where triplets of prime factors are circled in groups of three

topics.title: Cube Roots by Prime Factorisation
objectives: Student can calculate the cube root of a perfect cube using the prime factorisation method
Student can identify the unit digit of a cube root by observing the unit digit of its cube
visualIdeas: a table mapping the units digit of numbers to the units digit of their cubes, showing patterns like 2-to-8 and 3-to-7
a prime factorisation chain showing one factor pulled out from each group of three identical factors

topics.title: Cube Roots of Cube Numbers by Estimation
objectives: Student can estimate the cube root of a perfect cube number by dividing its digits into groups of three starting from the right
visualIdeas: a visual division of a six-digit cube number into two groups, showing how the first group gives the units digit and the second group gives the tens digit

topics.title: Recalling Ratios and Percentages
objectives: Student can convert ratios into percentages and vice versa
Student can calculate percentage increases and decreases in real-life quantities
visualIdeas: a comparative bar showing fractional parts, ratio, and percentage representation of the same quantity
a price tag showing a transition from old price to new price with the calculation of percent increase

topics.title: Finding Discounts and GST
objectives: Student can calculate discount and discount percentage based on Marked Price and Selling Price
Student can calculate the value-added tax or Goods and Services Tax (GST) and find the final billing amount
visualIdeas: an item tag showing Marked Price, Discount subtracted, and final Sale Price clearly labeled
a receipt breakdown showing Sales Price, GST percentage added, and final amount paid

topics.title: Prices Related to Buying and Selling
objectives: Student can calculate profit or loss percentage based on Cost Price and Selling Price
Student can solve multi-step problems involving overhead expenses added to the Cost Price
visualIdeas: a block diagram showing Cost Price + Overhead Expenses = Total Cost Price
a flow chart showing the formulas for Profit% and Loss% based on Total Cost Price

topics.title: Compound Interest
objectives: Student can differentiate between Simple Interest and Compound Interest with calculations over multiple periods
Student can calculate compound interest and amount using the standard formula for annual and semi-annual compounding
visualIdeas: a comparative line chart showing simple interest growing linearly while compound interest curves upwards over time
a table showing interest being added back to the principal at the end of each year to form the new principal

topics.title: Terms, Factors and Coefficients
objectives: Student can identify terms, factors, and numerical coefficients in a given algebraic expression
Student can classify expressions as monomials, binomials, trinomials, or general polynomials
Student can differentiate between like and unlike algebraic terms
visualIdeas: a tree diagram showing an expression branching into terms, and terms branching into numerical and variable factors
a sorting game style visual with different colored baskets for grouping like terms

topics.title: Addition and Subtraction of Algebraic Expressions
objectives: Student can add and subtract algebraic expressions by aligning like terms horizontally or vertically
visualIdeas: a column-wise addition grid where like variables are perfectly aligned vertically with space left for missing powers
a subtraction flow diagram showing how signs of the lower polynomial terms are reversed before adding

topics.title: Multiplication of Algebraic Expressions
objectives: Student can multiply a monomial by another monomial or three or more monomials
Student can multiply a monomial by a polynomial using the distributive law
Student can multiply two binomials or a binomial by a trinomial term-by-term
visualIdeas: an area model of a rectangle divided into four smaller boxes illustrating the multiplication of two binomials (x+a) and (y+b)
arched distribution lines connecting terms of a binomial to each term of a trinomial

topics.title: Standard Identities
objectives: Student can state the standard algebraic identities including (a+b)^2, (a-b)^2, (a^2-b^2), and (x+a)(x+b)
Student can apply these identities to calculate numerical products and simplify algebraic products efficiently
visualIdeas: a geometric dissection square of side (a+b) partitioned into squares of area a^2, b^2 and two rectangles of area ab
a worked example where 103 x 97 is transformed into (100 + 3)(100 - 3) and solved using the difference of squares

topics.title: Area of Trapezium and General Quadrilaterals
objectives: Student can calculate the area of a trapezium using the formula 1/2 * (sum of parallel sides) * height
Student can calculate the area of any general quadrilateral or a rhombus using diagonal lengths
visualIdeas: a trapezium split into a rectangle and two triangles, demonstrating the physical basis of its area formula
a general quadrilateral split by a diagonal into two triangles with perpendicular heights h1 and h2 labeled

topics.title: Area of a Polygon
objectives: Student can determine the total area of an irregular polygon by triangulating it or splitting it into trapeziums
visualIdeas: a field layout diagram (pentagonal or hexagonal) split into triangles and trapeziums with all raw measurements annotated along a central base line

topics.title: Surface Area of Cube, Cuboid and Cylinder
objectives: Student can differentiate between lateral/curved surface area and total surface area of cubes, cuboids, and cylinders
Student can calculate the surface area of cubes, cuboids, and cylinders to solve real-world packaging or painting problems
visualIdeas: the unfolded net views of a cuboid and a cylinder showing the flat shapes that form the total surface area
a cylinder net consisting of a rectangle with sides equal to height and circumference, and two circular bases

topics.title: Volume of Solids and Capacity
objectives: Student can calculate the volume of a cuboid, cube, and right circular cylinder using standard formulas
Student can convert between volume and capacity units such as cubic centimeters, cubic meters, milliliters, and liters
visualIdeas: a container filled with unit cubic blocks showing the space occupied (volume) compared with liquid filling (capacity)
a units conversion ladder showing links between 1 mL = 1 cm^3 and 1 m^3 = 1000 Liters

topics.title: Powers with Negative Exponents
objectives: Student can state the meaning of negative exponents as reciprocals of positive powers
Student can convert terms with negative exponents to positive exponents
visualIdeas: a pattern sequence showing powers of 10 decreasing: 10^2, 10^1, 10^0, 10^-1, 10^-2 with corresponding divisions by 10
a flip card visual showing a^-m becoming 1 / a^m

topics.title: Laws of Exponents
objectives: Student can apply exponent laws for multiplication, division, power of a power, and power of a product with integral exponents to simplify expressions
visualIdeas: a summary cheat-sheet graphic showing all laws of exponents with colorful examples for each rule
a step-by-step mathematical reduction where negative exponents are systematically simplified to positive exponents

topics.title: Use of Exponents to Express Small Numbers in Standard Form
objectives: Student can convert very small decimal numbers and very large numbers into standard scientific notation
Student can compare extremely small or large numbers by analyzing their exponent values
visualIdeas: an animation of a decimal point hopping over zero digits to the right, showing how the power of 10 decreases with each hop
a comparative slide of the size of a plant cell versus a red blood cell written in standard form

topics.title: Direct Proportion
objectives: Student can define direct proportion as a relation where the ratio of corresponding values remains constant
Student can solve real-life unitary problems involving direct variations, such as distance-time and map scales
visualIdeas: a table of values for gasoline volume and cost, demonstrating that x/y remains constant
a graph of direct proportion showing a straight line passing through the origin

topics.title: Inverse Proportion
objectives: Student can define inverse proportion as a relation where the product of corresponding values remains constant
Student can solve real-life problems where an increase in one quantity leads to a proportional decrease in another, like workers and days
visualIdeas: a diagram comparing 2 workers taking 6 hours with 4 workers taking 3 hours to complete the same wall
a value table where the product x * y is shown to be constant across all entries

topics.title: Factorisation by Common Factors and Regrouping
objectives: Student can express a monomial as a product of its irreducible factors
Student can factorise algebraic expressions by taking out common factors or by regrouping terms

color-coded regrouping steps showing binomial brackets becoming a common factor

topics.title: Factorisation using Identities
objectives: Student can factorise trinomial expressions using standard algebraic identities
Student can factorise quadratics of the form x^2 + (a+b)x + ab by splitting the middle term

topics.title: Division of Algebraic Expressions
objectives: Student can divide a monomial by another monomial by canceling common factors
Student can divide a polynomial by a monomial or another polynomial by factorising the numerator first

topics.title: Can you Find the Error?
objectives: Student can identify and correct common mathematical errors in algebraic expansions, substitution, and division

topics.title: Types of Graphs
objectives: Student can compare the uses of bar graphs, pie graphs, histograms, and line graphs
Student can interpret continuous changes over time represented by a line graph
visualIdeas: a grid presenting 4 different chart types for the same raw temperature data to show when each is best utilized
a temperature line graph showing peaks and valleys with specific coordinate points highlighted

topics.title: Linear Graphs and Coordinates
objectives: Student can plot a point on a Cartesian plane when given its coordinates (x, y)
Student can identify the coordinates of a plotted point by reading values from the axes

objectives: Student can construct graphs representing independent and dependent variables, such as quantity-cost or time-interest
